scenes.tts: A circuit formed without one protein. Switch the protein on in an adult. Can that undo the damage?
scenes.visual: Title card: Switch It Back On. The recurring synapse, its nucleus tag dimmed, beside a switch.
scenes.narration: A circuit formed without one protein. Switch the protein on in an adult. Can that undo the damage?

scenes.tts: Rett syndrome puts this to the test. Girls with it seem to develop typically for many months.
scenes.visual: A timeline of a girl's early development, typical for many months.
scenes.narration: Rett syndrome puts this to the test. Girls with it seem to develop typically for many months.

scenes.tts: Then they lose purposeful hand use and speech.
scenes.visual: The timeline turns: icons for hand use and speech fade.
scenes.narration: Then they lose purposeful hand use and speech.

scenes.tts: Most cases come from mutations in one gene, meck P two, on the X chromosome.
scenes.caption: Most cases come from mutations in one gene, MECP2, on the X chromosome.
scenes.visual: An X chromosome with MECP2 marked near one end.
scenes.narration: Most cases come from mutations in one gene, MECP2, on the X chromosome.

scenes.tts: Its protein binds methylated D N A, and is thought to help set the level of many genes.
scenes.caption: Its protein binds methylated DNA, and is thought to help set the level of many genes.
scenes.visual: The protein, MeCP2, sits on D N A at methyl tags; dials beside several genes turn up or down a little.
scenes.narration: Its protein binds methylated DNA, and is thought to help set the level of many genes.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking the gene appear typical for several weeks. Then they develop tremor, breathing changes and reduced movement.
scenes.visual: A mouse timeline: typical for weeks, then symptom icons for tremor, breathing and movement.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking the gene appear typical for several weeks. Then they develop tremor, breathing changes and reduced movement.

scenes.tts: Their neurons do not die in large numbers. They are smaller, with simpler dendrites.
scenes.visual: Two neurons side by side: typical, and smaller with simpler dendrites. Label: alive, but small.
scenes.narration: Their neurons do not die in large numbers. They are smaller, with simpler dendrites.

scenes.tts: In two thousand seven, Jacky Guy, Adrian Bird and colleagues built mice in which the gene is silent.
scenes.caption: In 2007, Jacky Guy, Adrian Bird and colleagues built mice in which the gene is silent.
scenes.visual: Credit: Guy, Bird and colleagues, 2007. The gene drawn with a blocking sequence inside it.
scenes.narration: In 2007, Jacky Guy, Adrian Bird and colleagues built mice in which the gene is silent.

scenes.tts: A blocking sequence silences it. The mice also carry an enzyme, Cree.
scenes.caption: A blocking sequence silences it. The mice also carry an enzyme, Cre.
scenes.visual: The blocking sequence between two lox P sites. A Cre enzyme waits outside the nucleus.
scenes.narration: A blocking sequence silences it. The mice also carry an enzyme, Cre.

scenes.tts: Cree enters the nucleus only after the drug tamoxifen is given. Then it cuts out the block.
scenes.caption: Cre enters the nucleus only after the drug tamoxifen is given. Then it cuts out the block.
scenes.visual: Tamoxifen arrives; Cre enters the nucleus and cuts the block out. The gene lights up.
scenes.narration: Cre enters the nucleus only after the drug tamoxifen is given. Then it cuts out the block.

scenes.tts: Predict. If the circuit was built wrong for good, what does restoring the protein in a sick adult do? And if it only needs the protein to run?
scenes.visual: Text on screen: Predict. Symptom score over time, with a tamoxifen arrow at adulthood; the curve after it is hidden.
scenes.narration: Predict. If the circuit was built wrong for good, what does restoring the protein in a sick adult do? And if it only needs the protein to run?

scenes.tts: Many symptoms reversed, in young adult mice and in older adult mice.
scenes.visual: The symptom score falls after tamoxifen, for young adult and older adult mice.
scenes.narration: Many symptoms reversed, in young adult mice and in older adult mice.

scenes.tts: In typical mice, tamoxifen did nothing.
scenes.visual: A flat control line. Label: typical mice plus tamoxifen.
scenes.narration: In typical mice, tamoxifen did nothing.

scenes.tts: So circuits that formed without the protein can work again once it returns. That does not show their development was normal.
scenes.visual: The grid from chapter one: restore late, yes. Small note: not proof of normal development.
scenes.narration: So circuits that formed without the protein can work again once it returns. That does not show their development was normal.

scenes.tts: Now the other test. In two thousand eleven, Huda Zoghbi's laboratory deleted the gene in adult mice.
scenes.caption: Now the other test. In 2011, Huda Zoghbi's laboratory deleted the gene in adult mice.
scenes.visual: Credit: Zoghbi laboratory, 2011. A typical adult mouse; the gene is cut out.
scenes.narration: Now the other test. In 2011, Huda Zoghbi's laboratory deleted the gene in adult mice.

scenes.tts: They developed symptoms like those of mice that never had it. The protein is needed continuously.
scenes.visual: Symptom icons appear in the adult mouse. The grid fills: delete late, yes.
scenes.narration: They developed symptoms like those of mice that never had it. The protein is needed continuously.

scenes.tts: Both late tests point the same way. The adult circuit still needs this protein. A building role is not ruled out.
scenes.visual: The grid from chapter one: restore late, many symptoms improve; delete late, symptoms appear. Label: needed in adults; building role not ruled out.
scenes.narration: Both late tests point the same way. The adult circuit still needs this protein. A building role is not ruled out.

scenes.tts: The balance of excitation and inhibition shifts too, and in one brain it runs both ways. The forebrain tends to be underactive. The brainstem tilts toward excitation.
scenes.visual: A mouse brain map: forebrain shaded as underactive, brainstem shaded as tilted toward excitation.
scenes.narration: The balance of excitation and inhibition shifts too, and in one brain it runs both ways. The forebrain tends to be underactive. The brainstem tilts toward excitation.

scenes.tts: One limit. This is a mouse result. Whether it holds for an older person is not known.
scenes.visual: Card: a mouse result.
scenes.narration: One limit. This is a mouse result. Whether it holds for an older person is not known.

scenes.tts: A second limit. The dose matters. Too much of this protein causes a separate syndrome in males.
scenes.visual: A dose bar with too little on one side and too much, duplication, on the other; a working range in the middle.
scenes.narration: A second limit. The dose matters. Too much of this protein causes a separate syndrome in males.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: some traits can still be reversed, and some proteins are still needed in adults. The late tests ask both questions.
scenes.visual: Closing card: Built, then kept. The filled grid. Labels: reversible? still needed?
scenes.narration: Takeaway: some traits can still be reversed, and some proteins are still needed in adults. The late tests ask both questions.
